Right: To be told the grounds of arrest as soon as may be
Source: FC Art 5(3); CPC s.28A(1); SOSMA s.4(2)
Why_It_Matters: Defines whether you are arrested at all and what the case is; Red Book: arrest without grounds is unlawful

Right: To be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours (excluding necessary journey)
Why_It_Matters: Hard ceiling on police-only detention; triggers judicial scrutiny

Right: To consult and be defended by a lawyer of your choice
Why_It_Matters: Questioning must be deferred for a reasonable time; consultation out of hearing

Right: To inform a relative or friend of your whereabouts
Why_It_Matters: Prevents incommunicado detention; enables family to engage counsel

Right: Not to be arrested merely as a witness
Source: CPC s.23(1) (no witness ground); s.111 route
Why_It_Matters: Most common misuse in everyday encounters

Right: To walk away when not under arrest and no stop power is invoked
Source: FC Art 5(1), Art 9(2); CPC s.15 (what arrest is)
Why_It_Matters: Red Book 2.3 test: 'Am I under arrest?'

Right: To refuse to answer self-incriminating questions in a s.112 examination and to remain silent after a DDA caution
Why_It_Matters: Core protection in police questioning

Right: To make representations (personally or through counsel) at remand and to have reasons recorded
Why_It_Matters: Only point where detention is judicially tested; raise ill-treatment here

Right: Remand capped at 4+3 days (<14 yrs) or 7+7 days (death/14+ yrs)
Why_It_Matters: Prevents open-ended investigative detention

Right: To be searched only by an officer of the same sex, with strict regard to decency
Why_It_Matters: Express in every regime reviewed

Right: Not to be strip-searched unless arrested, on reasonable suspicion, with Inspector's prior approval, in private
Why_It_Matters: Replaces the Red Book's 'no law' statement with concrete conditions

Right: To be present during a search of your premises and to receive a signed list of everything seized
Why_It_Matters: Principal safeguard against planting and loss of property

Right: To see the search warrant before entry to a closed place
Why_It_Matters: Enables on-the-spot validity check (court, seal, address, scope)

Right: Not to be subjected to more restraint than necessary; no hurt or confinement to extort a confession
Why_It_Matters: Criminalises coercive interrogation; confessions so obtained are irrelevant

Right: To have a confession to police below Inspector or in police custody excluded (general rule)
Why_It_Matters: Limits evidential value of custodial 'admissions' (displaced for DDA s.37B, SOSMA s.18A, MACC, AMLA)

Right: To refuse directions of a non-uniformed officer who will not declare office and produce ID (road context)
Source: RTA s.123(2); PA s.14 certificate of appointment
Why_It_Matters: Protects against impersonation; Red Book authority-card colours

Right: Not to have your vehicle searched without reasonable grounds, or detained beyond what the search needs
Why_It_Matters: Most frequent search encounter

Right: Habeas corpus: High Court must inquire into any complaint of unlawful detention
Why_It_Matters: Ultimate remedy for detention beyond limits (even SOSMA s.4 does not oust Art 5(2))

Right: Mandatory Magistrate's inquiry into any death in police custody
Why_It_Matters: Accountability mechanism for families

Right: Equal protection regardless of nationality; immigration 14-day rule applies only to immigration-law detention
Why_It_Matters: Prevents misuse of the immigration window for criminal investigations
